1. SCOPE

t.i This standard (Part I ) prescribes the hygienic requirements for fish holds, handling of fish on hoard and transport of fish from fishing VeSSf"J to the processing sitc.
2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard the following- definitions shall npply.
2.1 Boxed Stowage vessel (Jee 2.8). 'The stowage of Iish on board of the vessel in boxes.

2.2 Bulk Stowage - The Blass stowage of fish in pounds OIl board the
2.3 Chilling - The process of cooling fish to a temperature approaching that of melting ice.

2.4 Fillet ---.. A slice of fish of irregular size' and shape removed from the
carcass by cuts made to the backbone.

2.5 Fish -- Any or the cold-blooded aqu.u ic: vcrtebrntr animals, Pisces,
Elasmobracks and Crustacea
(Jff

IS: 7313-1~)7~ * ).

2.6 Fresh Fish - Freshly caught fish wh ir h have received no preserving treatment, or which have been preserved only hy chilling.

2.7 Gutted Fish - Fish frorn which the guts have been removed.
2.8 Pound. or Pens - Areas in the fish hold and on deck, divided off by
stanchions and portable board structures for the storage of fish.

2.9 Shelf Stowage - The stowage of fish in single layers, on shelves on
hoard of the vessel.

3. HANDLING OF FRESH FISH AT SEA
3.1 Fishing Vessel Facilities and Operating Requirements

3.1.1 General Considerations 3.1.1.1 Fishing vessels should be designed for the rapid and rfficicnt handling of fish, case of cleaning and sanitization, and should hi?' of such material and construction as not to cause any damage or contamination to the catch. 3.1.1.2 Fishing vessels should be so designed and constructed as not to cause contaminauon of the fish with IJiJgc, sewage, smoke, fuel, oil, grease or other objectionable substances. Fish should be protected against physical darnag�, exposure to high temperatures and drying effects of sun and wind.

3.2 Sanitary Facilities

3.3 Equipltlent and Utensils
3.3.1 All fish handling, conveying and sf OJ age cqlliprllcnt, used on board of fishing vessels. shouk! be designed for the rapid and �Ilicir-nt handling of fish. 3.3.7 The fishing vessels should be equipped with lirushr-s , scrapers, water hoses, spray nozzles and other suitable washing and sanitizing equipment.
3.4 Hygienic Operating Requirements 3.4.1 Before any fish is brought aboard, and between each haul of the gear, decks, boards, stanchions and all other deck equipment which may come in contact with fish should be hosed down with clean sea-water and brushed to remove all visible dirt, slime and blood. 3.4.2 All tuhs, tanks, barrels and other equipmcnt llsrd in the handling, gutting, \vashillg and conveying OPC) .uions should }H' thoroughly cleaned after such cycle of operations.

7

IS : 4303 ( Part 1 ) � 1915
3.4.3 During fishing- trips the fish hold bilge sump should be drained regularly. 'The sump should be accessible at all times. 3.4.4 Cod ends and other parts of the fishing gear which COOle in contact with fish should be freed of dead fish and orga nic material after each haul. All gear should be thoroughly cleaned after fishing operations. 3.4.5 Sea-water which has been used for cooling engines, condensers or similar equipment should Hot be used for washing fish, deck, hold or any equipment corning in contact with fish. 3.4.6 When cleaning and hosing operations arc carried out while the vessel is in port, potable fresh or clean sea-water should be used. 3.4.7 Irnrnediatelv after the catch is unloaded, t he deck and all deck equipment. should l~(' hosed clown, brushed, thoroughly cleaned with a suitable cleaning agent, and sanitized. 3.4.8 I mmediatcly after the catch is unloaded, the fish hold and bilge sump should also he ern pt icd completely. All surfaces in the 1101d, pound boards and surnp should be thoroughly cleaned with a suitable cleaning agent, and sanitized. 3.4.9 In ships using refrigerated sea-water or refrigerated brine systems for the prcserva tion of the catch) all tanks, plllnps, heat exchangers and other associated equipment should be cleaned immediately after discharging the catch. Potable water containing a suitable cleaning ag('nt should be circulated through all parts of the system, 'ranks should be inspected carefully and cleaned out by brushing, if necessary. 3.4.10 Where refrigerated sea-water is used for the preservation of fish, only clean sea-water should be used and should be changed as often as possible to prevent the accumulation of contaminating materials. 3.4.11 Adequate precautions should be taken to ensure that the human and other wastes from the fishing vessel arc disposed of in such a manner as not to constitute a public health hazard. 3.4.12 Effective measures should be taken to protect the fishing vessel against insects, rodents, birds or other vermin. 3.4.13 Dogs, cats and other domestic animals should he excluded from areas of the vessel where fish is received, handled, processed and stored. 3.4.14 After catching species, such as herring for reduction purposes, when a vessel is converted for storing fish in icc for human consum ption, the hold shall he thoroughly cleaned, and sanitized. 8

3.5 Handling the Catch on Board
3.5.1 Duration of the fishing trip for a fishing vessel should be determined by the facilities available on the vessel for handling and keeping the catch well-chilled, distance from the processing plant and t he local environmental conditions.

3.5.2 Handling of the catch should begin as soon as it

COlllCS

on board.

3.5.3 \rVhere it is required to keep species of fish unsuitable for human consumption, these should always hr" sorted It"On1 the edible catch and kept separate at all times,

3.5.4 Fish should not be trampled or stood upon, and should not be piled deeply on deck.
3.5.5 All fish on deck should be protected from sun, frost, and the drying effects of wind.

3.5.6 Line-caught fish should, wherever practicable, be stunned as soon as they arc taken on board the vessel.
3.5. 7 Bleeding of the fish, when necessary, should be done immediately after the fish is landed.
3.5.8 Gutting of the fish should commence immediately on arrival of the catch on the deck.

3.5.9 Where rapid gutting is not prarticnblc, whole fish should he washed and chilled as soon as it arrives on deck. 3.5.10 As it is impracticable to gut very small fish, these should be placed in iced and chilled storage quickly.
3.5.11 C;uttillg should be complete and carried out with care.

3.5.12 Fish guts should not be allowed to contarninate other fish on deck.

3.5.13 Separate and adequate storage facilities should be provided for the fis h roc, milt and li vel'S if these are I equ ired to be sa ved for uti lization later. 3.5.14 Immediately after gutting ~ fish shou1<1 be washed with cold clean sea-water and further handling should be carried out without delay.

3.5.15 Deck hatches should not be left open longer than necessary to load the fish which should be allowed to slide down the chutes into the hold or be lowered in suitable containers.
3.5.16 Fish should be chilled rapidly in melting icc and should be stored so that the tcrnpcraturc does not rise. For short term storage, refrigerated sea-water or refrigerated brine may be used.

9

is I 4303 ( Part I ) � 1975
3.5.17 Fish in ice should be stowed in shallow layers. 3.5.18 The practice of shelf stowage is not recommrndcd , unless the single layers of fish are completely covered wit h layers of icc. 3.5.19 Fish should be surrounded by adequate quantities of ice. 3.5.2.0 Ice should also be used to prevent contact with all surfaces in the fish hold. 3.5.21 Crushed icc should always be used to give close contact with

the fish.
ted brine
3.5.22 Fish should not be packed in refrigerated sea-water or refrigera3 to a density of n101'C than UOO kgjrn �

3.6 Unloading the Catch 3.6.1 The catch should be unloaded carefully without little delay.
3.6.2 At the conclusion of each fishing tri p, all unused icc should be removed Irorn the fishroorn before cleaning. 3.6.3 'I'he catch of different days should not be mixed. 3.6.4 Mechanical unloading equipment should be used where possible and care should be taken to avoid damage during unloading. 3.6.5 The catch should be unloaded into clean containers and imrnediately placed in a suitable covered area. While laying III this area. the catch should be maintained in a chilled condition. 3.6.6 Care should be taken that fish are not damaged or contaminated during sorting, weighing and transfer to containers. 3.6.7 In case the unloading of refrigerated brine or sea-water boats is carried out by means of punlps and syphons the compensating or ' Makeup' water should be of the same temperature and quality as the original brine.

4. CARE AFTER UNLOADING
4.1 Care shall be taken to avoid any damage or injury to fish. 4.1 The fish shall not be exposed to the sun or rain. 4.3 Fish de-iced for weighing shall be re-iccd or chilled below 2�; within one hour from unloading.

5. TRANSPORT FROM THE UNLOADI!'lG SITE TO TIlE
PROCESSING UNIT 5.1 Fresh Fish S.I.1 Fresh fish, which has been chilled, shall not be transported or accepted [or transport when the internal product temperature exceeds 2"C,

10

IS : 4303 ( Part I ) � 1975
5.1.2 Containers used Ior the transport of fresh fish shall not be fi lied to an extent as to cause damage to the fish when containers arc placed one above the other. 5.2 Frozen Fish - Frozen fish shall be continuously maintained at a temperature of -1 B"C or below during transport except for short intervals during loading and unloading when the ternpcrat ure of the fish shall not exceed -'.' 12()(~ and the fish shall be cooled to -1 B0C as quickly as possible.

S.3 Other General Provisions
5.3.1 All vehicles and containers used in the transport of fish shall be so constructed as to be easily cleanable. 1\lat.crials used for li ning shall be of metal or other rnaturial impervious to water. 'rile floor of the vehicle shall be constructed of durable matcrin l impervious to water. All corners shall be rounded to facilitate cleaning. 5.3.2 Before and after the transport of fresh Iis h, fish containers and the carrying compartment of vehicles shall be waslivcl , and the floors of vehicles scrubbed with cold water and a suitable detergent anti then rinsed with clca n fresh water. -5.3.3 All cquiprnent, receptacles a nr] conta incrs cOIning in contact with fish shall be washed and scrubbed daily with clean water and a suitable detergent. After cleani ng with detergents all surfaces of the carrying cornpartmcnt of the vehicles and equipment shall be rinsed wit h clean fresh water. 5.3.4 Fresh or frozen fish for human consum ption shall not he transported in containers or vehicles where spoilage or contarni nat iou is likely to occur from contact wit h other goods. Fish offal shall not be transported with fish meant for human consumption. 5.3.5 Before loadi ng with fish, all int.erior sur[lces of vehicles and containers shall be clean and shall IH~ free froIll objectionable odours characteristics of spoiled fish. 5.3.6 Transport vehicles and containers shall be maintained in good condition and regular checks shall be made on the thermal efficiency of the insulated or refrigerated carrier. 5.3.7 I nsulatcd container and vehicles equipped with refrigeration shall be pre-cooled to an air temperature of _7 or below before commencemerit of loading. 5.3.8 Frozen fish shall he loaded in a refrigerated transport vehicle in a manner that provides for the free circulation of air at the top, bottom and sides of the load. A minimum air space of 75 mm from the top, 25 mJP from the floor and ) 2~5 rnrn from each.of the. sides .shall be provided. 5.3.9 After the loading or unloading operations, the mechanical refrigeration equipment shall be turned on and the doors of containers and vehicles shall be kept closed.

6. THE RECEIVING POINT
6.1 Immediately on receipt from a fishing boat or transport vehicle, fish to be processed or packed as fresh fish shall be chilled by packing in ice or by other suitable method so that the temperature does not exceed 2�C but is in no case lower than -- 2':)C. Fish to be preserved or packed as quick frozen or deep frozen fish shall be processed immediately on unloading or chilled to a temperature not exceeding 2�C~ hut in no case lower than -2�(:. 6.2 Fish held before processing shall be placed in clean well-drained bins, boxes or containers. 6.3 Prior to processing, loose fish shall be kept in clean containers or on a clean smooth surface with a slope for suitable drainage.

6.4 All fish shall be adequately washed with clean water prior to processing and before packing.

7. EMPLOYEE HYGIENE
7.1 Every person employed for fish handling on the fishing vessels shall he medically examined by an authorized registered medical practitioner and the examination shall include X-I{ay of the chest Ior tuberculosis. The examination shall also include exarni nat ion of stoul for protozoal and helminthic infestation for those parasites which are transmitted by ingestion, and for the presence of Salmonella, Shigella species and Vibrio cholerae; urine; and blood examination for venera] diseases. Subsequcnt ly , an employee shall be medically examined once in a year or more frequently, j f necessary, to ensure that he is rnedicallv fit and free from communicable diseases. A record of such exarni nat ion s'hall be maintained.

7.1.1 It shall be impressed on all employees that they should tlotify the medical officer or management, cases of fever, sore throat, of cough, vorni ting, diarrhoea, typhoid, dysentery, boils, cuts and sores and ulcers (howe\'cr small ), discharging ears and notifiable diseases occurring ill their own homes and families, 7.1.1 No worker who is suspected to be suffering f1'o111 any oft.he disorders listed in 7.1.1 shall be permitted to work inside the unit unless found medically fit. The supervisor shall check t he personal hygiene of the workers before the start of work and whenever they enter any processing room after any absence. 7.2 Employees shall keep their 'finger nails short and clean and wash their hands with soap or detergent and water be-fore commencing work and after each absence, specially after using senitary conveniences. Towels used Ior drying hands should be clean. No worker shall allow his clothing and/or any part of his/her body other than his/her hand from elbow downward to
